title: The effect of AI-powered chatbots in social studies education
extended_summary:
This study examines whether an AI-powered chatbot can improve learning outcomes in middle school Social Studies and how students and the teacher experience its use. The paper addresses a gap identified by the authors: while chatbots have been studied in language and computer science education, their use in Social Studies had not previously been investigated.

The intervention was a closed-domain, hybrid chatbot called SosyalciBot, built with Dialogflow and MindBehind. It provided short instructional explanations, question-answer activities, hints, instant feedback, motivational messages, visual support, and some audio-based delivery. The chatbot was integrated into 6th-grade Culture and Heritage lessons, sometimes used before teacher instruction to build readiness and sometimes after teacher instruction to reinforce learning. A pilot was conducted, and then the main study used a pretest-posttest control group quasi-experimental design with three intact classes: one experimental group and two control groups taught with a constructivist approach. Quantitative outcomes were measured with a researcher-developed achievement test and a delayed permanence test five weeks later; qualitative data came from interviews with 17 students and the practitioner teacher.

Results showed that the experimental group outperformed both control groups on post-test and retention measures, with large effect sizes. Interview data suggested the chatbot improved readiness, engagement, enjoyment, and reinforcement of learning, and both students and the teacher viewed it as a useful teaching support. Participants especially valued the chatbot’s instant feedback, constructive language, visual and audio support, and opportunities for repeated practice. Limitations were also noted, including lack of voice input, limited dynamism, and the need for stronger AI communication capacity. Overall, the paper concludes that chatbots have strong potential for Social Studies education, but further refinement is needed for broader and more flexible classroom use.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general AI-powered chatbot used for instructional dialogue, lesson explanation, question-answering, hints, instant feedback, and reinforcement in a closed-domain educational setting.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as 'SosyalciBot' to teach and reinforce 6th-grade Social Studies content, provide Q&A practice, clues, instant feedback, and motivational support; deployed in both written and audio forms in a web-based platform.

findings.finding_summary: In a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design with 78 6th-grade students, the experimental group taught with the chatbot scored significantly higher on the post-test than both control groups after adjusting for pretest scores. The corrected post-test means were 20.897 for the experimental group, 17.027 for Control 1, and 16.478 for Control 2; the group effect was significant with F(2,74)=7.646, p=.001, η²=.171.
findings.measure: 6th Grade Culture and Heritage Success Test post-test scores (ANCOVA-adjusted)

findings.finding_summary: On the delayed permanence test, the experimental group again outperformed both control groups after adjustment for pretest scores. The corrected permanency-test means were 21.944 for the experimental group, 18.394 for Control 1, and 17.233 for Control 2; the group effect was significant with F(2,74)=9.019, p<.001, η²=.196.
findings.measure: 6th Grade Culture and Heritage Success Test permanency test scores (ANCOVA-adjusted)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods quasi-experimental study with one nonrandomly assigned teacher/classroom implementation and qualitative interviews, not a randomized trial. The design is credible for classroom intervention evidence, but there are no subgroup analyses or randomized controls to raise the tier higher.
impact_tier_rationale: The adjusted group effects were statistically significant and in the modest-to-large range (η²=.171 and .196). This indicates meaningful positive impact on academic outcomes for the chatbot-assisted instruction.
